facts.statement: Altispinax was a large predatory theropod dinosaur that lived between 140 and 133 million years ago in what is now East Sussex, England.
facts.quote: Altispinax (; "with high spines") is a genus of large predatory theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Berriasian - Valanginian, 140 to 133 million years ago) of what is now the Wadhurst Clay Formation of East Sussex, England.

facts.statement: Fossil collector Samuel Husbands Beckles discovered nodules containing dinosaur bones near Battle, East Sussex, probably in the early 1850s.
facts.quote: Probably during the early 1850s, fossil collector Samuel Husbands Beckles discovered some nodules with dinosaur bones in a quarry near Battle, East Sussex.

facts.statement: Richard Owen reported the fossils discovered by Samuel Husbands Beckles in 1856.
facts.quote: These he sent to palaeontologist Richard Owen, who reported them in 1856.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Altispinax is catalogued as NHMUK PV R 1828 and dates to the late Valanginian age.
facts.quote: The fossil, now catalogued as NHMUK PV R 1828, was probably found in a layer of the Hastings Bed Group dating from the late Valanginian age.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Altispinax consists of three posterior dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: It consists of a series of three posterior dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene named the genus Altispinax in 1923 based on three vertebrae with high spines that he considered distinct from Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1923 Friedrich von Huene created a separate genus for Megalosaurus dunkeri. He used the three vertebrae as the basis for this genus, noting that they were different from Megalosaurus, and created the name Altispinax (meaning "with high spines") based on their appearance.

facts.statement: Gregory Paul tentatively estimated in 1988 that Altispinax weighed 1 tonne and was shorter than the 8-meter-long type specimen of Acrocanthosaurus atokensis.
facts.quote: Paul in 1988 tentatively estimated that Altispinax weighed 1 tonne (1.1 short tons) and was shorter than the type specimen of Acrocanthosaurus atokensis which measures about 8 meters (26 ft) long.

facts.statement: Ralph Molnar suggested that the two vertebrae closest to the skull in Altispinax are fused.
facts.quote: According to Ralph Molnar the two spines closest to the skull are ankylosed or fused.

facts.statement: Ralph Molnar interpreted the fusion of the front spines as evidence of an injury to a back frill that healed from behind.
facts.quote: This Molnar explained as a result of injury to a back frill, the wound later closing from behind.

facts.statement: Darren Naish proposed in 2003 that the gap between the front spines was natural rather than the result of injury.
facts.quote: In 2003, Darren Naish gave a different interpretation, suggesting the gap was natural.

facts.statement: The classification of Altispinax is debated, with placements ranging from Eustreptospondylidae to Allosauroidea, though most researchers currently place it in Tetanurae incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Olshevsky originally assigned Altispinax to the Eustreptospondylidae. In 2003 Naish considered it a member of the Allosauroidea. Most researchers give a less precise placement as Tetanurae incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Altispinax was once considered a nomen dubium because no relationship could be proven between the type vertebrae and a single tooth previously assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: Later researchers considered Altispinax a nomen dubium because the single tooth was undiagnostic. No relationship could be proven between the tooth and the vertebrae.

facts.statement: George Olshevsky named the genus Becklespinax in 1991 for the Altispinax vertebrae to honor the original discoverer, Samuel Husbands Beckles.
facts.quote: For this reason, in 1991 a new genus, Becklespinax, was named for the vertebrae by George Olshevsky, in honour of the original discoverer, Beckles.

facts.statement: Four additional species were named within the genus Altispinax before being reclassified into other genera.
facts.quote: Four other species would be named within the genus Altispinax.

facts.statement: Olshevsky transferred the species Altispinax oweni to the separate genus Valdoraptor in 1991.
facts.quote: In 1991 Olshevsky created a separate genus Valdoraptor for this species.

facts.statement: The species Altispinax parkeri was given the separate generic name Metriacanthosaurus in 1964.
facts.quote: This species in 1964 was given the separate generic name Metriacanthosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Altispinax was established by von Huene in 1923.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Altispinax is Altispinax dunkeri.

facts.statement: Altispinax lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 133 million years ago in the Valanginian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a los comienzos del período Cretácico hace 133 millones de años, en el Valanginiense en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: The type species Megalosaurus dunkeri was originally described and named by Wilhelm Barnim Dames on December 16, 1884, during a conference.
facts.quote: Su especie tipo, Megalosaurus dunkeri, fue descrita y nombrada originalmente por Wilhelm Barnim Dames el 16 de diciembre de 1884 durante una conferencia

facts.statement: The species name honors paleontologist Wilhelm Dunker, who discovered the tooth in Deister years prior.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra al paleontólogo Wilhelm Dunker, quien, varios años antes, había descubierto el diente en Deister

facts.statement: The holotype was added to the University of Marburg collection under catalog number UM 84.
facts.quote: Este holotipo fue añadido por él a la colección de la Universidad de Marburg bajo el número de catálogo UM 84

facts.statement: In 1923, Friedrich von Huene created a separate genus for Megalosaurus dunkeri, naming it Altispinax.
facts.quote: En 1923, Friedrich von Huene creó un género separado para Megalosaurus dunkeri: Altispinax

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the Latin "altus" meaning "high" and the Neo-Latin "spinax" meaning "with spines".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del latín "altus" que significa "alto" y el neolatín "spinax", es decir "con espinas"

facts.statement: The name was inspired by specimen BMNH R1828, a series of three dorsal vertebrae with very high spines referred to the species by von Huene.
facts.quote: El nombre fue inspirado por el espécimen BMNH R1828, una serie de tres vértebras dorsales con muy altas espinas que von Huene refirió a la especie

facts.statement: It is debated whether Altispinax is valid, as later research suggested the type specimen, a tooth, was not diagnostic, making it a nomen dubium with no probable connection to the spines.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en la segunda mitad del se cayó en cuenta de que el espécimen tipo alemán, el diente no era diagnóstico lo que convierte a Altispinax en un nomen dubium sin ninguna conexión probable con las espinas

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul proposed a separate species for the vertebrae series, tentatively assigning it to Acrocanthosaurus as ?Acrocanthosaurus? altispinax.
facts.quote: En 1988 Gregory S. Paul creó una especie separada para la serie de vértebras, que él asignó a Acrocanthosaurus como ¿Acrocanthosaurus? altispinax

facts.statement: In 1991, George Olshevsky named the independent genus Becklespinax for these vertebrae.
facts.quote: Por tanto, en 1991 George Olshevsky nombró un género independiente Becklespinax para estas vértebras

facts.statement: In 1923, von Huene renamed Megalosaurus oweni to Altispinax oweni based on metatarsal NHMUK 2559.
facts.quote: En 1923 von Huene renombró a Megalosaurus oweni Lydekker 1889, basándose en el metatarso NHMUK 2559, como Altispinax oweni

facts.statement: In 1991, Olshevsky created the genus Valdoraptor for the species formerly known as Altispinax oweni.
facts.quote: En 1991 Olshevsky creó el género Valdoraptor para esta especie

facts.statement: In 1932, von Huene renamed Megalosaurus parkeri to Altispinax parkeri.
facts.quote: En 1932 von Huene renombró a Megalosaurus parkeri Huene 1923 como Altispinax parkeri

facts.statement: In 1964, the species formerly known as Altispinax parkeri was given the new genus name Metriacanthosaurus.
facts.quote: A esta especie se le dio en 1964 un nuevo nombre de género, Metriacanthosaurus

facts.statement: The name Metriacanthosaurus is considered a modern synonym of Becklespinax.
facts.quote: Este nombre sería un sinónimo más moderno objetivo de Becklespinax

facts.statement: Altispinax belongs to the parent group Theropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Theropoda

facts.statement: Altispinax is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
